notes: Source of truth for Talon scam categories. Weights blend T-Mobile's 2023 Scam and Robocall Report (call-based) with common text-scam lures; they are our estimates, not measured text shares.

harm_types.money: Victim sends money or gift cards
harm_types.credentials: Victim enters a password, PIN or one-time code
harm_types.personal_info: Victim gives SSN, Medicare number, date of birth or similar
harm_types.account_takeover: Scammer ports the number or takes over a carrier or bank account

decoy_tactics.play_confused: Misunderstand on purpose so the scammer repeats and restates details
decoy_tactics.ask_callback_number: Ask for a number to call back, so a phone indicator gets sent
decoy_tactics.ask_link_again: Say the link did not open and ask for it again or for another site
decoy_tactics.ask_who_to_pay: Agree to pay, then ask exactly where and to whom
decoy_tactics.payment_trouble: Stall with payment trouble so the scammer offers another method
decoy_tactics.ask_company_details: Ask for company name, department, agent ID or case number
decoy_tactics.accept_next_step: Go along and ask what the next step is
decoy_tactics.issue_tripwire: Hand over a mock trackable gift card code or wallet (FR-14)

shared_next_steps: Don't reply or tap any link.
Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM) to report it.
Contact the company using its official app or the number on your card or statement, not the one in the message.

categories.name: Medicare and health insurance
categories.description: Fake Medicare, ACA or insurer messages: card replacement, free benefits, enrollment deadlines.
next_steps: Medicare won't text you for your Medicare number. Call the number on your own card if unsure.

categories.name: Fake bank fraud alert
categories.description: Fake bank or card alerts about a suspicious charge that push a link, a callback or a 'refund' over a payment app.
next_steps: Your bank will never ask you to move money to a 'safe' account. Call the number on your card.

categories.name: Package delivery
categories.description: Fake carrier notices about a failed delivery or address problem that ask for a small redelivery fee.
next_steps: Track packages only in the carrier's official app or site using your tracking number.

categories.name: Unpaid toll or fine
categories.description: Fake unpaid toll, parking or DMV fine notices with a late fee threat.
next_steps: Check balances on your toll agency's or DMV's official site, typed in yourself.

categories.name: Retail order or refund
categories.description: Fake order confirmations, refunds or account holds from retailers.
next_steps: Check your orders in the retailer's app. Never install software for a refund.

categories.name: Government impersonation
categories.description: Fake IRS, Social Security or other agency messages about refunds, benefits, debts or legal action.
next_steps: Government agencies don't demand payment by text or gift card. Go to the agency's official .gov site yourself.

categories.name: Carrier impersonation and SIM swap
categories.description: Fake T-Mobile or other carrier messages: expiring reward points, outage credits, account suspension, or requests for a port-out or verification code.
next_steps: T-Mobile won't ask you to confirm sensitive info in an unsolicited text. Check your account in the T-Life app.
Never share a verification code or account PIN with anyone.
If you tapped the link, change your T-Mobile ID password.

categories.name: Tech support and account lockout
categories.description: Fake tech company, streaming or antivirus messages about a locked account, a hack or a subscription renewal.
categories.targets: Adults 55+ for tech support; all ages for lockouts
next_steps: Real tech companies don't text you to call support. Never let anyone remote into your device.

categories.name: Job and task scams
categories.description: Unsolicited remote job offers, often 'task' work that later requires deposits to unlock earnings.
next_steps: Real employers never ask you to pay to start or unlock earnings.

categories.name: Investment and crypto
categories.description: Crypto or stock tips, 'mentor' groups and fake trading platforms, often after a long trust-building chat.
next_steps: No legitimate investment guarantees returns. Don't send crypto to anyone you met by text.

categories.name: Wrong number and romance
categories.description: A friendly 'wrong number' or flirty opener that builds a relationship, then moves to investment or money requests.
next_steps: Be careful with strangers who text 'by mistake' and keep chatting. Never send money to someone you haven't met.

categories.name: Family emergency
categories.description: 'Hi Mom, new number' or grandparent scams claiming a relative needs urgent money; may use cloned voices.
next_steps: Call your family member on the number you already have before sending anything.

categories.name: Prize, lottery and giveaway
categories.description: Claims you won a prize, gift card or sweepstakes, with a fee or details needed to claim it.
next_steps: Real prizes never require a fee to claim.

categories.name: Debt relief and loans
categories.description: Pre-approved loans, debt forgiveness or student loan relief that charge upfront fees.
next_steps: Legit lenders don't charge upfront fees by text. Check student loans only on the official federal site.

categories.name: Fake charity and disaster relief
categories.description: Donation requests or fake aid after disasters and in the news.
asks: donation via payment app or crypto
categories.targets: All ages; people in affected areas
next_steps: Donate through the charity's official website, typed in yourself.
